A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UB-GOLD and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Matching datasets and experiments support reliable comparison despite appendix renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmarking results for 16 methods across 35 datasets, including detection performance, near/far OOD detection, contamination robustness, and computational efficiency.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds evaluations of AAGOD and GOODAT, additional robustness metrics, and detection-score distribution analyses.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a new detector, and no algorithmic revision to the retained methods is established. AAGOD and GOODAT are added comparison methods; the new framework diagram and theoretical objectives do not establish a changed training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: The same 35 dataset configurations and four anomaly/OOD scenarios remain. The near/far and contamination experiments retain their datasets, and the new score-distribution analyses reuse existing benchmark data rather than introducing new task coverage.

E2.justification: AAGOD and GOODAT move from cited work to evaluated comparators in Tables 3, 7, and 8 and the robustness and efficiency comparisons, introducing the pretrained-GNN comparison family. Figure 8 additionally brings IG-iF, IG-SVM, GCL-iF, and GCL-SVM into the contamination comparison, which previously reported only end-to-end methods.

E3.justification: v2 extends contamination evaluation to AUPRC and FPR95 and supplies search ranges for the newly evaluated AAGOD and GOODAT in Table 4. Existing dataset splits, contamination levels, near/far sample counts, search budgets, and efficiency procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 8–10 broaden robustness analysis across methods and metrics. Appendix F.3 and Figure 12 add score-separation case studies for ten methods on four existing dataset configurations. Figure 11 instead reorganizes existing benchmark results by method family; it is not a new controlled ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five runs with varying random seeds and report means and standard deviations in Table 8. v2 extends this existing reporting practice to additional methods without introducing new run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results for AAGOD and GOODAT, additional robustness metrics, and score-distribution findings. The original 16 methods' per-dataset Table 8 values remain unchanged, while reported aggregate ranks change. Table 7 swaps OCGTL's ZINC far/near AUROC from 84.40/99.58 to 99.58/84.40, with corresponding AUPRC/FPR95 swaps, resolving its disagreement with v1 Figure 3.

T1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix D.1 add threshold classifiers and idealized expected-score separation objectives in Equations 1–6, without theorems or proofs. The new equations assign lower scores to OOD graphs, conflicting with the retained Definition 1 statement that larger scores indicate OOD.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion expand the claimed comparison from 16 to 18 methods, and the conclusion adds score-distribution analysis. The central unified-benchmark contribution, 35-dataset scope, and principal cross-task findings remain.

C2.justification: New appendices substantially expand interpretations: Appendix A argues for unsupervised graph-level evaluation, F.2 attributes performance differences to method mechanisms and pretraining dependence, and F.3 interprets score overlap as detection difficulty. F.1 newly qualifies contamination conclusions as metric-dependent. Section 5 removes the earlier exclusion of methods requiring class labels.

D1.justification: Table 4 adds AAGOD and GOODAT hyperparameter ranges; Appendix B adds explicit split-separation and node-attribute information. A new footnote describes pretraining generically but leaves the actual pretrained configurations unclear. Hardware, software versions, repository access, licensing, and existing implementation information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including BOND, GADBench, and ARC, alongside newer graph-learning citations. Appendix A adds positioning relative to node-level benchmarks and computer-vision OOD evaluation. The established unified-benchmark novelty claim remains; AAGOD and GOODAT were already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain. v2 renames generalizability to OOD sensitivity spectrum, expands library and dataset explanations, reorganizes the appendices, and adds ethics and acknowledgments while removing the checklist. These are targeted expansions rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds the benchmark overview, supplementary robustness plots, method-family displays, and a 40-panel score-distribution figure. Existing comparison tables and plots expand to accommodate additional methods, and Table 1 gains anomaly ratios. The document also adopts ICLR formatting and substantially rearranges appendix displays.

improvement.justification: Expanded comparisons, multi-metric robustness evidence, and score-distribution diagnostics improve breadth, while Table 7 resolves an existing table–figure disagreement. However, the new equations contradict the stated score direction, and new numerical claims introduce inconsistencies: Section 4.1 cites an ES→MU best AUROC of 99.64 although Table 3 shows 92.41; GOODAT's PROTEINS AUROC also differs between Tables 3 and 8. Together with insufficiently specified pretraining for the added comparators, these reliability concerns prevent a confident net quality judgment.
